findings.title: canManage() grants on VIEW scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). An admin holding only the view scope on all groups is therefore treated as able to manage groups. addTopLevelGroup calls requireManage(), so a view-only admin could create top-level groups. The check should accept MANAGE only.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Groups resource-type resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission, if the group resource is not found, the Groups resource-type resource is loaded. getResourceTypeResource can return null: V2 not enabled, a different resource server, or the resource not yet created. The result is passed straight to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and then to resource.getScopes() without a null check, so it can throw an NPE. The same applies to the individual-group lookup that falls back to this path.

findings.title: Group ID collected from the resource instead of its name
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds groupResource.getId(), which is the authorization resource's own UUID. The group ID is the resource name, because getOrCreateResource names the resource after the group id. The returned IDs are then used in user searches filtered by group, so they will not match any group. hasPermission is also called with the resource id, but it looks the resource up by name, so the lookup fails and falls through to the all-groups path. It should use getName().

findings.title: V1 group-based user search no longer filtered for restricted admins
findings.body: searchForUser no longer guards the group-ID lookup with !auth.users().canView(). GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission still returns an empty set when users().canView() is true. That keeps the behavior in the V1 common case. However, the V1 canView() now checks only roles and no longer treats grantIfNoPermission as a grant, which differs from before. This should be verified.
